title: Independent differentials make the p-root quotient a finite field
statement: Let $k$ be a field of prime characteristic $p$, $n\ge0$, $a:\operatorname{Fin}n\to k$, and assume the differentials $\mathrm da_i$ in $\Omega_{k/\mathbf F_p}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] are $k$-linearly independent. For the actual quotient $Q=k[X_i]/(X_i^p-a_i)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pth-root-algebra-local], $Q$ is a field, is finite-dimensional over $k$, and every $x\in Q$ satisfies $x^p\in\operatorname{im}(k\to Q)$.

source.place: Tag 07E5, proof of (2) => (4), first paragraph; Algebra 07DZ; monic division for the reduced-monomial bound. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07E5 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07DZ (local checkout absent).

proof.text: Choose roots alpha_i in an algebraic closure of k. The existing degree theorem makes their intermediate field F finite-dimensional of dimension p^n. The reduced-monomial bound makes Q finite with dimension at most p^n.

Evaluation kills the defining ideal and induces g:Q->Omega. Its range equals F as a subalgebra, since the algebraic field adjunction equals the algebra adjunction and the polynomial evaluation range equals the latter. Restricting g to F gives a surjective linear map. Its dimension inequality forces dim Q = dim F and then injectivity. Transport the field property through this algebra isomorphism.

The quotient is nontrivial by the isomorphism and inherits characteristic p. Induct on a polynomial representative using constants, sums and multiplication by X_i. Frobenius preserves sums, and q(X_i)^p=a_i reduces the multiplication step; hence every p-th power is a coefficient.

theorem pthRootAlgebra_isField_finite_pow
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p]
    (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → k) :
    letI := ZMod.algebra k p
    LinearIndependent k (fun i ↦ KaehlerDifferential.D (ZMod p) k (a i)) →
    let Q := pthRootAlgebra p n k a
    IsField Q ∧ Module.Finite k Q ∧
      ∀ x : Q, x ^ p ∈ (algebraMap k Q).range
